title: Malloreddus alla Campidanese
subtitle: Sardinian saffron pasta with sausage and tomato
excerpt: Malloreddus alla campidanese is the defining dish of the Campidano plain in Sardinia: small ribbed saffron pasta dumplings in a rich tomato and pork sausage sauce, finished with pecorino. The saffron in the pasta is a Sardinian signature -- Sardinia is the only Italian region that produces saffron commercially.
sourceNotes: Malloreddus (also called gnocchetti sardi) are a traditional Sardinian pasta made from semolina and saffron. Alla campidanese refers to the style of the Campidano plain, using local pork sausage and Sardinian pecorino. The dish is the representative pasta of Sardinia.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce improves if made the day before.

content.text: Malloreddus are made from semolina and water with a pinch of saffron dissolved in the water. The dough is stiffer than egg pasta and takes more kneading. The shape is formed by pressing a small piece of dough against a ridged gnocchi board or the back of a fork and rolling it forward. Good dried gnocchetti sardi from Italian delis is a reasonable substitute if making the pasta from scratch is not feasible.

Mix {{semolina}} semolina with the saffron water (from {{saffron}} saffron dissolved in warm water) and a pinch of {{salt-table}} salt. Knead for 10 to 15 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Break off small pieces of dough (about 8g each). Press each piece against a gnocchi board or fork tines and roll to form ridged oval shapes. Place on a semolina-dusted tray.

Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat. Brown {{sausages-pork}} sausage meat, breaking it up, for 5 minutes. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 1 minute. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and let it bubble. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tomatoes and season with {{salt-table}} salt. Simmer for 25 minutes until thick.
Cook the malloreddus in well-salted boiling water for 3 to 4 minutes until tender. Drain and toss in the sauce. Add {{basil}} basil if using. Serve with {{pecorino}} pecorino.

items.symptom: The pasta dough is too stiff to knead
items.cause: Semolina absorbs water more slowly than 00 flour.
items.fix: Add water a teaspoon at a time until the dough is workable. Semolina dough should be firm but not crumbly. Rest it fully before shaping -- it becomes more pliable after resting.

content.text: Malloreddus alla campidanese is the national dish of Sardinia. The Campidano plain, the broad agricultural valley in southern Sardinia, produces the saffron used in the pasta and the pork sausage used in the sauce. Sardinia is the only Italian region that grows saffron commercially. The dish is served at every celebration on the island: weddings, christenings, and harvest festivals.
